summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic back pain was admitted with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and hyperglycemia leading to diabetic ketoacidosis. The episode was likely triggered by recent emotional stress after disclosing childhood sexual abuse. She was managed in the ICU with IV fluids and insulin, then transitioned to the medicine floor. Her insulin regimen was adjusted due to hypoglycemia, reducing Lantus from 24 to 17 units nightly. Gabapentin was restarted for chronic pain at a low dose to avoid exacerbating gastroparesis. Nausea improved with supportive care and resumption of metoclopramide. A urine culture showed coagulase-negative staph without signs of infection, so no antibiotics were given. She stabilized, tolerated a full diet, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for diabetes management, mental health support, and medication adjustments.
